crime_highlights: There she drove the vehicle at Joanne Bernard, striking her in the legs and lower stomach
Joanne Bernard was pinned between the accused’s vehicle and another parked car
the accused reversed, striking Martha Stevens in the legs
Joanne Bernard was six months pregnant
Joanne Bernard had bruising to her legs and lower belly and a sore back
Martha Stevens had bruising to her legs and a swollen knee requiring a brace for three weeks
rationale_highlights: I think Gladue helps to understand and define the public dimension here

The situation of the offender, her past and present position in her community, the initiative she has shown in advancing her own education, and her potential to be an example to young people in classrooms in first nations communities are therefore especially persuasive factors
I have concluded that the public interest is better served by granting a conditional discharge
note: Gladue used to support a conditional discharge, not causal.

Gallant kicked in the door and he and A.S. entered the house
He hit her on the head with a flashlight, causing the flashlight to break. She started to moan. He punched her in the face.
At that point Gallant kneed her in the face
A.S. knew that Gallant had entered Lavinia Campbell’s bedroom

rationale_highlights: His personal circumstances are difficult to separate from his aboriginal heritage
his paternal family has been subject for generations to systemic discrimination and neglect
A.S. cannot be held to be as responsible for his actions as someone whose life experiences are more conducive to the development of moral judgment
A.S.’ background is considered in assessing his level of moral blameworthiness
Because of his background, including his Maliseet heritage, his sentence should reflect a lesser degree of moral blameworthiness
note: Young person; manslaughter, party to break-in where Gallant killed victim.

crime_highlights: The key aggravating factor here is the serious nature of these offences
theft of a substantial quantity of inventory destined for the Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation
there is an economic cost here in terms of the loss of use of property and the retail-sale value of the unrecovered merchandise
Mr. Maloney’s degree of responsibility was substantial
the substantial degree of planning and calculation that was obviously involved in carrying out a heist of this magnitude
rationale_highlights: Another mitigating factor is the important information relayed to the Court by Mr. Sutherland regarding Mr. Maloney’s aboriginal background
The Court takes judicial notice of the broad, systemic, cultural and background factors affecting members of First Nations communities who come into conflict with the law
The Court also takes into account the case-specific information that has been provided helpfully today by Mr. Sutherland
note: Very brief Gladue treatment; no victim harm described, property offence.
